clue.text: Make a formal speech to the dancers, as one might do before driving off.

definitions.text: Make a formal speech to the dancers
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to speak formally to the guests gathered at a grand formal dance

definitions.text: as one might do before driving off
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in golf, a player takes a stance over the teed-up sphere just before a drive

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on from 1-across into 6-across. 'Driving off' sounds like leaving the party by car, but it is a golfer teeing off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally for a speech to a dance gathering and idiomatically for a golfer's set-up routine before swinging.

clue.text: See 28 across
Put his feet down and up around the guy not working now.

indicators.note: the reversed word is wrapped around the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, putting one's feet down
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A man stamps about angrily around a fellow who has just lost his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive or idle for the time being, like a sleeping volcano.

clue.text: What's the point to a crazy duel when you get to escape by trickery?

parts.note: E is east, one of the points of the compass

indicators.note: a crazy arrangement scrambles the letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why anyone would fight a mad duel when they could sneak away instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like the purpose of the duel, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or slip away from someone, often through cunning or dodging.

clue.text: Not out, and not finishing typing what might relate to a holding force on the baby's necessity?

definitions.text: what might relate to a holding force on the baby's necessity

parts.note: in baseball or cricket a player who is not out is safe

indicators.note: the word typing is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A rambling picture of an unfinished typing job somehow connected to holding a baby's needs in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The baby's necessity is a cloth diaper, which was held in place by this kind of fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is the clasp with a guarded point once used to fasten a cloth diaper (nappy) on an infant.

clue.text: Just a favorite part-time activity, but gets a little shot in the barge.

indicators.note: the pellet abbreviation sits inside the word for the barge

parts.note: a hoy is an old type of heavy barge or coastal sailing vessel
BB is the small pellet fired from an air rifle, a BB gun

explanation.surface: Someone's pastime turns into a shooting incident aboard a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: HOY is an archaic vessel that crops up in crosswords far more than on rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is a leisure pursuit taken up for pleasure in one's spare time.

clue.text: See 1
Possibly coy maneuver of the CIA, which proves out of date.

parts.note: arch means playfully knowing or coy, so coy is one possible sense of it

indicators.note: to maneuver the agency's initials is to shift them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller scene in which a shy-seeming agency trick turns out to be hopelessly old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coy' looks like a description of the maneuver, but 'possibly coy' is a sideways definition of a short word for knowing or mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something antiquated, belonging to an earlier era and no longer in use.

clue.text: Black doesn't start to desire the queen, due to a ho-hum appearance.

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective, or the old noun for a lack of shine

indicators.note: the word black loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
lust is strong desire
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A chess game where black, slow off the mark, covets the queen and the play looks dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture of Black and the queen is a red herring; Black only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackluster means dull and uninspired, lacking any shine or vitality, which is what a ho-hum look conveys.

clue.text: Hauled in bad parlance the essential part for one who might dish out a dose.

definitions.text: one who might dish out a dose

parts.note: drug is a dialect or nonstandard past tense of drag, so it means hauled in sloppy speech
the gist is the core or essence of something

explanation.surface: Someone hauls in the core of a badly worded speech for a person handing out medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bad parlance' flags the nonstandard form, as in 'the cat drug it in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A druggist is an American pharmacist, who dispenses medicines in measured amounts to customers.

clue.text: It's crazy, fame! Fur makes this winter warmer.

indicators.note: calling the words crazy says their letters are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about celebrity, then a remark that fur keeps you warm in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earmuff is one of a pair of padded covers worn over the ears to keep them warm in cold weather.

clue.text: At the end of labor, the CIA improperly has a large number making a kind of acid.

parts.note: the closing three letters of the word labor

indicators.note: the agency's initials are placed out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A union-busting tale in which the spy agency improperly takes on a big workforce, all in an acid bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the last three letters of a word, rather than one, is a loose but fair reading of 'the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boracic acid is another name for boric acid, the mild antiseptic made from boron.

clue.text: The Bayeux example is noted, but you get certain recordings with effort.

parts.note: tapes are recordings made on magnetic tape
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A note that the famous Bayeux work is celebrated, and that making recordings takes work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is the long embroidered cloth showing the Norman conquest of England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bayeux work is the best-known instance of an embroidered wall hanging of this type.

clue.text: The quest for one is legendary, with a large number going by what the train runs on.

definitions.text: The quest for one is legendary

indicators.note: the first piece goes beside the next, the two joined end to end

parts.note: G stands for grand, a thousand dollars
a train runs along a rail

explanation.surface: A legendary quest set aboard a railway, with crowds of passengers passing by.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand, a thousand, is American slang and a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is the cup sought by King Arthur's knights in medieval legend.

clue.text: Commanded the unknown symbol to end up plentiful! (You shouldn't set one for the kids!)

definitions.text: You shouldn't set one for the kids

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
x is the usual symbol for an unknown quantity in algebra
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: An order to make an algebra problem come out generously, followed by a parent's warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like setting a math problem, but it is setting an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents are urged to set a good example to children, never a poor model of behavior for them to copy.

clue.text: A broken-down stair gets you moving!

indicators.note: the stair is broken down into a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A collapsing staircase gets you going in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion or activity.

clue.text: One from Italy accompanies a Scotsman to present one from Bucharest.

indicators.note: one piece keeps company with the next, placed side by side

parts.note: a Roman is a person from Rome, in Italy
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scotsman's name

explanation.surface: An Italian travels with a Scot to introduce a Romanian friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital of Romania, so a native of that city is a Romanian.

clue.text: Turns out to be around what many a business tacks on its name, but they're found away from big cities.

definitions.text: they're found away from big cities

indicators.note: the first word goes around the abbreviation placed inside it

parts.note: something that turns out a certain way proves so

parts.words: what many a business tacks on its name
parts.note: Inc., short for incorporated, follows many American company names

explanation.surface: A reflection on companies that turn out to be based in the countryside rather than in big cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The provinces are the regions of a country outside its capital and major cities.

clue.text: It's not "in," and more insensitive, to have more fighters on your side!

definitions.text: to have more fighters on your side

parts.note: the opposite of in is out
number here is the comparative of numb, meaning more lacking in feeling

explanation.surface: Being unfashionable and unfeeling is apparently a way to get more soldiers in your army.
explanation.walkthrough: Number reads as the counting word, but it is numb plus -er; that is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber the enemy is to exceed them in count, having more troops than they do.

clue.text: A small cafe in Paris makes the state troubled about what belongs to me.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the other piece, enclosing it
a troubled word has its letters stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged
what is mine belongs to me

explanation.surface: A little Parisian cafe gets the nation into a fuss over my possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro, a word also familiar from First World War soldiers.

clue.text: Likely found at elevenses, or at 4 pm, but teacher loses her art to prove it!

definitions.text: Likely found at elevenses, or at 4 pm

indicators.note: the word teacher gives up the letters of the word that follows it

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are removed
taken as written: these are the letters taken away
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher gives up her art to prove a point about mid-morning and afternoon snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is the British mid-morning snack break and 4 pm is afternoon teatime, when food comes round on this wheeled trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cart is a small wheeled table used for serving tea and refreshments, often brought out at snack time.

clue.text: "Sir," for example–submit it legally for show.

indicators.note: the run of letters is on show within these words, spanning their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of submit, the whole of it and the start of legally

explanation.surface: An instruction to present a knight's honorific through proper legal channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submit it legally' reads like filing a document, but the letters sit in plain view across those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is a form of address and an honorific, granted to knights, which counts as a title.

clue.text: Traveler–stout, disheveled–moves around the little, very little state.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters move around the abbreviation, enclosing it
a disheveled word has its letters tousled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged
RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state

explanation.surface: A portly, scruffy traveler wanders all over a tiny state.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island is the smallest of the fifty states, hence 'very little'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a person traveling for pleasure, visiting places of interest.

clue.text: What? Not a loss once more!

wordplay.note: the opposite of a loss is a gain, written here with its article

explanation.surface: A disbelieving exclamation that, once again, there has been no loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Not a loss' as 'a gain' and run the two words together; 'What?' is a puzzled exclamation that leads in.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, repeated on another occasion.

clue.text: You'll have to praise a number, to start with, to find another number–from poppies!

parts.note: to laud is to praise
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening part of the word number is used

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like instruction to praise a figure first in order to arrive at another figure derived from poppies.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'number' is read as numb-er, something that numbs: an opiate painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is a tincture of opium, which is extracted from poppies, and was used as a painkiller and sedative.

clue.text: The tattooed lady is disturbed daily.

indicators.note: a disturbed word has its letters thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tattooed woman suffers some upset every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lydia, the Tattooed Lady' is a 1939 comic song made famous by Groucho Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: The song names its heroine Lydia, so the title character is identified by the epithet in the clue.

clue.text: City in Italy rises where there's room at the top.

definitions.text: where there's room at the top

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: citta is the Italian word for city

explanation.surface: An Italian city climbs to where there is space at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in Italy' wants a place name like Rome or Turin; it is the Italian word for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space immediately under a house's roof, the topmost room.

clue.text: See 28 across
Almost all play has a club, for example — and this might advertise it.

indicators.note: nearly the whole word play, missing only its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened
a club is one suit of playing card, so a club is an example of a card

explanation.surface: Most of a stage play features a nightclub, and a poster might promote the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightspot or a golf club; it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a printed notice or poster displayed in public to announce or promote something.

clue.text: Diamond enthusiasts might want to have them. (Cotton or wool to confirm with confidence how old you are!)

definitions.text: Diamond enthusiasts might want to have them

parts.note: batting is cotton or wool wadding in sheets, used for quilts
to aver is to state firmly as true
your age; ages is the plural

explanation.surface: A baseball fan's wish list, then an aside about using fabric to swear to your age.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from 28-across into 1-down and 26-down. The diamond is the baseball field, not a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball fans follow batting averages, each hitter's ratio of hits to times at bat, as a key statistic.

clue.text: Newt might be an example of such, and get left so they can display it.

definitions.text: Newt might be an example of such
definitions.note: the definition names a single creature; the answer is plural, the kind it belongs to

indicators.note: the words that follow hold the answer in plain view across their join

parts.note: the letters run from inside left across into so

explanation.surface: A hint that Newt, the politician, is one of a kind that gets dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newt' hints at Newt Gingrich, but it is the amphibian; 'and get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A young newt in its land-living stage is called an eft, so a newt is an example of the creature.

clue.text: Makes up the material on a sort of seat.

indicators.note: in an across answer the material sits on, alongside, the next piece

parts.note: fabric is cloth, material

indicators.note: a sort of seat is a version of the word with its letters sorted afresh

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An upholsterer covers a chair with cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes up' looks like assembling a chair cover, but it means inventing a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to invent or concoct something false, just as one makes up a lie.
